{{Short description|Dutch structural biologist (1932–2022)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=December 2023}}
'''Johan Nomdo Jansonius''' (1932 – 2 January 2022) was a Dutch chemist and structural biologist. He spent his career at the [[Biozentrum University of Basel]] where he was professor of structural biology between 1973 and 1998.

==Life==
Jansonius was born in the Netherlands in 1932.<ref name=rug>{{cite web|url=https://hoogleraren.ub.rug.nl/hoogleraren/1205-jansonius-johan-nomdo |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201012200427/https://hoogleraren.ub.rug.nl/hoogleraren/1205-jansonius-johan-nomdo |title=Johan Nomdo Jansonius (1932) |language=nl |publisher=University of Groningen |date= |archive-date=12 October 2020}}</ref><ref name="obit">{{cite web|url=https://www.biozentrum.unibas.ch/news/detail/obituary-for-johan-n-jansonius-1932-2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230417023518/https://www.biozentrum.unibas.ch/news/detail/obituary-for-johan-n-jansonius-1932-2022 |title=Obituary for Johan N. Jansonius (1932 - 2022) |publisher=biozentrum.unibas.ch |date=11 January 2022 |archive-date=17 April 2023}}</ref> He studied chemistry.<ref name="obit"/> Jansonius obtained his PhD from the [[University of Groningen]] in 1967 with a thesis titled: ''"De kristalstructuur van papaïne : een röntgendiffractie-onderzoek met een oplossend vermogen van 4,5 Å"''.<ref name=rug/> He subsequently was lector of [[protein structure]] chemistry at the same university between 1971 and 1973.<ref name=rug/> He was professor of [[structural biology]] at the [[University of Basel]] between 1973 and 1998 and introduced the field of [[protein crystallography]] there.<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.biozentrum.unibas.ch/research/emeriti-former-professors/emeriti/johan-n-jansonius/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201012201027/https://www.biozentrum.unibas.ch/research/emeriti-former-professors/emeriti/johan-n-jansonius/ |title=Prof. Dr. Johan N. Jansonius, Emeritus |publisher=University of Basel |date= |archive-date=12 October 2020}}</ref> He joined the newly founded [[Biozentrum University of Basel]], of which he later served as chair from 1989 to 1991.<ref name="obit"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.biozentrum.unibas.ch/about/biozentrum-at-a-glance/history/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180828134708/https://www.biozentrum.unibas.ch/about/biozentrum-at-a-glance/history/ |title=The Biozentrum – its history and role |publisher=Biozentrum University of Basel |date= |archive-date=28 August 2018}}</ref>

He was one of the founders of the field of [[crystallography]] in Switzerland. Apart from his work in the field of protein crystallography he performed research on [[enzyme]]s related to [[metabolism]]. Jansonius looked into the [[vitamin B6]] dependent enzymes and their structure-function relationship. He clarified the structure of five of those enzymes. Jansonius also worked on [[Thermophile|thermophilic]] enzymes.<ref name="obit"/>

Jansonius was elected a corresponding member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1988.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/correspondents/4306 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200812212409/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/correspondents/4306 |title=Johan Jansonius |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |archive-date=12 August 2020}}</ref> He died on 2 February 2022 in [[Therwil]], Switzerland, aged 89.<ref name="obit"/>
